caption: A cat crouches on a kitchen floor, jumps up onto the counter, and lands on it.

sa.check: A cat crouches on a kitchen floor.
The crouch comes first, then the jump, then the landing.

pc.expect: It pushes off with its hind legs, arcs upward, and lands front paws first.
pc.fail: It floats up; or lands before it has jumped; or rises straight up and hangs.

pc.expect: Its legs fold and extend at the joints and the body stretches in the air.
pc.fail: A leg detaches; or the body stretches like rubber; or the legs bend mid-bone.

pc.expect: After the peak it comes down onto the counter and stays.
pc.fail: It hovers; or rises through the ceiling; or bounces high off the counter.

pc.expect: Its paws land on the counter top.
pc.fail: It passes through the counter; or sinks into it; or the counter passes through the cat.

pc.expect: One cat keeps its shape and stays one cat.
pc.fail: It splits; or merges with the counter; or turns into another animal.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The cat's markings and the kitchen stay the same.
pc.fail: The markings change; or the kitchen rearranges; or the counter changes.

note: The cat is self-driven: the timing of its jump is its own. Only the arc and the body's integrity are judged.
